summary: Kittitas County, WA lookout on Polallie Ridge: cabin about 1921, 25-ft L-4 tower 1936/37, ended 1947 or 1965 (sources differ); footings remain in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness.

facts.design: Log cabin with open-air cupola (about 1921), replaced by a 25-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Register says it is now gone; Willhite's photos show a footing and an old cabin foundation on the site

access.note: Hiking route inside the Alpine Lakes Wilderness; no closure or restriction is described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Pete Lake Trail, then Tired Creek Trail 2.3 miles to the ridgetop, then 0.2 miles on the Polallie Ridge Trail; road paved until its last mile of good gravel (Willhite)

events.note: Log cabin with open-air cupola, developed about 1921 (register and firelookout.com); Willhite says 'early 1920s'
Wenatchee Daily World item, as quoted on washingtonlookouts.weebly.com, said a lookout cabin would be built on Polallie Ridge that year
Clifford Stipp named as lookout personnel by firelookout.com; no other staffing named in the sources read
Register and firelookout.com say a 25-ft pole L-4 replaced the cabin in 1936; Willhite dates the tower to 1937
Register and firelookout.com say abandoned in 1947; Willhite says the inventory suggests 1947 but images show it still around afterward
Firelookout.com only ('burned in 1965'); Willhite cites a 1964 hiking guide that mentions the lookout and a 1965 map label
Registered October 28, 2012 as US 1419, WA 319; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com say the 25-ft L-4 tower replaced the cabin in 1936; Willhite gives 1937. Both are kept in the events.

The register says abandoned in 1947 and gone; firelookout.com says burned in 1965; Willhite says the inventory suggests 1947 but later images show the lookout still there. The story reports all three.
The register and firelookout.com call it Polallie Mountain; Willhite calls it Polallie Ridge Lookout Site. Both give an elevation of 5,482 feet, so they are the same site.

notes_for_editor: Brief access was 'unknown'; the record now says public (hiking route in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness). Brief record needed no corrections. The 1930 newspaper item is not confirmed as the same cabin as the 1921 one. The 1965 burn rests on firelookout.com alone. No new photos were recorded: the NPS and picryl images were seen only in search snippets, not fetched.
